title: Choking Response
summary: How to respond to airway obstruction in adults and children.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Assess the Situation
sections.body: Ask the person 'Are you choking?' If they can speak, cough, or breathe, encourage them to cough forcefully to clear the obstruction. Do not interfere with their attempts to cough.
sections.warning: Do not give a choking person water or food, as this can worsen the blockage.
sections.image_description: Person nodding and coughing while holding throat

sections.heading: Step 2 — Deliver Back Blows
sections.body: If they cannot speak or breathe, bend them forward at the waist and support their chest. Deliver five sharp blows between the shoulder blades using the heel of your hand.
sections.warning: Ensure the person is bent forward so the object exits the mouth rather than sliding further down.
sections.image_description: Rescuer giving back blows to bent-over person

sections.heading: Step 3 — Perform Abdominal Thrusts
sections.body: If the blockage is not cleared, stand behind the person. Wrap your arms around their waist. Make a fist with one hand, place it slightly above the navel, and grasp it with the other hand. Press hard into the abdomen with a quick upward thrust. Repeat up to five times.
sections.warning: Do not perform abdominal thrusts on pregnant women or infants under 1 year. Use chest thrusts instead.
sections.image_description: Rescuer performing Heimlich maneuver from behind

sections.heading: Step 4 — Call for Help and Start CPR
sections.body: If the person becomes unconscious, lower them gently to the ground. Call emergency services immediately. Begin CPR, starting with chest compressions. Each time you open the airway, look for the object and remove it if visible.
sections.warning: Never perform blind finger sweeps as you may push the object deeper.
sections.image_description: Person lying down receiving chest compressions

when_to_use: When someone is choking, cannot speak or breathe, or is clutching their throat (the universal sign of choking).
do_not: Use abdominal thrusts on infants under 1 year
Hesitate to call emergency services if the object remains stuck
sources: International Red Cross First Aid Manual
